checks.detail: No lock waits: no session is blocked.

audit.report: A replayable batch job (batch_replayable_inventory, pid 1000456) sat idle in transaction for 4.2 seconds holding locks that blocked all checkout sessions, driving checkout success to 0% over 30 seconds with $18,400/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian proposed termination; the Continuity Guardian required change-calendar evidence, which showed no active window covering the job. After the second proposal included that evidence, both guardians agreed to terminate. The executor killed the blocker, and within 10 seconds checkout recovered to 100% success (36/36) with no lock waits and no protected settlements affected. The business is back within its 60-second degradation tolerance.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_inventory job (pid 1000456) was idle in transaction (last statement SELECT 1) holding locks that blocked all checkout sessions.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory, pre-fetch change-calendar coverage in the incident runbook to avoid a round-trip probe during negotiations.
Add monitoring and alerting for batch_replayable_inventory workers that go idle in transaction longer than 2 seconds to catch the application bug that left it stuck on SELECT 1.
Set a lock_timeout or statement_timeout on the batch_replayable_inventory role so the job self-terminates if it holds locks idle beyond a safe threshold.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian proposed correctly with full evidence in round 1; the Continuity Guardian properly enforced the change-calendar invariant, causing a one-round delay only because that evidence was not pre-fetched. No guardian wasted a round or missed evidence beyond the required invariant check.
follow_ups: Update the incident runbook for batch_replayable_inventory to include an automatic change-calendar check at detection time.
Investigate the application code path that leaves batch_replayable_inventory idle in transaction on SELECT 1 and fix the transaction boundary.
Configure a lock_timeout of 5s for the batch_worker role running batch_replayable_inventory to prevent future lock contention.

proposal.rationale: Root blocker pid 1000456 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory) has been idle in transaction for 4.2s with last statement SELECT 1, holding locks that block checkout sessions [DB-1]. Checkout success is 53-72% vs 95% SLO with ~$5,175/min revenue at risk and business tolerance of only 60s degraded checkout [TEL-1, BIZ-1]. The workload name 'batch_replayable_inventory' suggests replayability, but workload_registry and protected_settlements probes are needed to confirm interrupt safety and settlement impact before execution.

proposal.risk_assessment: If the workload is not actually replayable or has high replay cost, termination could cause data inconsistency or require expensive manual recovery. If protected card settlements are in flight under this session, termination could disrupt payment processing. Need registry and settlements probes to quantify.
